title: Modus II: from printed letters to German

facsimile.region_note: Printed p. 57 is HAB image 249 and corpus image 251. The detail shows the significant letters and the beginning of the cover text. The full page also shows the alphabet and the German Intentio.

passage.label: German Intentio in the reading edition
passage.note: The printed German appears in the apparatus at this passage.

cover.label: Exemplum secundi (cover prose sample)
cover.method: Printed p. 56 directs the writer to begin with an empty word, then alternate. In the opening of the cover on p. 57, the decorated initial belongs to Creator. The line break in guberna has been joined and the abbreviation in consequamur expanded.

cipher_stream.label: Literae significantes
cipher_stream.method: The archived transcription is retained in its previous order and spelling. Its periods delimit individual letters in this edition. The printed line is set in spaced italic type. No individual human transcriber is documented here.

extraction.rule: Take the initials of the second, fourth and subsequent even-numbered cover words. For the separate significant-letter stream, read the recorded letters in order and remove the editorial separators.

decode.rule: The print moves each plaintext letter two places back on its 22-letter circle. Invert the 22 printed pairs and substitute for each cipher letter in sequence.

intentio.diplomatic: Ich bitte dich komm von stund an zu mir/ es thut sehr noth.
intentio.translation: I beg you, come to me at once; it is very urgent.
intentio.normalization: Lowercase the German, omit spaces and punctuation, and write u as v for comparison.

editorial_note: The retained stream decodes to 42 letters. Its opening gafz gives ichb. The resulting text differs from the 45-letter normalized Intentio, beginning at position 6. The sources of the remaining differences are unresolved.
provenance: Frankfurt, 1608, Herzog August Bibliothek Wolfenbüttel, Fb 243. Printed p. 56 describes the shift and diagrams the circle. Printed p. 57 gives the paired alphabet, German intention, significant letters and cover.
AI visual collation on 23 November 2026 checked the two pages, all 22 substitutions and the first fourteen cover words. Human verification of this correction is undocumented.
The full significant-letter transcription is the pre-correction input. The displayed result is computed from that input without supplying letters from the printed intention.
